chapter: Sid Leprotti and the So Different band
title: The So Different Band and its dead members; Paul Howard
summary: The So Different band of 1919 with Slocum Williams and the Spike brothers, the Black and Tan band, and who is still living.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, well, he worked all over. Yeah. And that's why I said he could have been here, or up in Canada, or somewhere. The band was called So Different. Mm-hmm. And I had the Spike Brothers and... I'll tell you last night. Mm-hmm. The Black and Tam Band, and they and themselves were so different. Did I tell you that? No, I don't remember who the Black and Tam? Yeah, they and themselves were so different. And the SIDS Band was so different, because they had Slocum Williams. He's from New Iberia, Slocum. He's dead. He was a clarinet player. He was a clarinet player.
There was only six of them.
You know, Dick Johnson recorded a piece for me once. I may put out some records of it years ago. I think for many years.
He's some kind of Jellie Roll.

Yeah, his brother-in-law. Mm-hmm. And Dick, one piece he played, sort of the slow blues. And I said, what's the name of that? He said, well, call it the So Different Blues. And I thought that was a funny name, but I never know it came from the band. I wondered where he got that. He never didn't mean much to me.

Well, I was out there in 1919. Who? I said, well, I was out there in 1919. Yeah. They called it Band of So Different Band. Mm-hmm. They all died out there, folks. Yeah, both of the Spike brothers dead. Slocum's dead. Cheryl Green, he's dead? Yeah. And Doc was the drummer. He got killed in the tube over there, Stockton Tunnel, rather. They all was dead, and Sid's the only one left. And he's about to pass. How's that fight? How's that? Harris Sutherland, he's living? Who? Harris Sutherland. Oh, no, Harris wasn't dead. He's the one who had the black and tan band in love. And that band, yeah. Yeah, he's the barber. Uh-huh. And how about Minnie? Who? Well, we called Minnie out here. He came out here and he called his man. What do you mean? Ernest Johnson. Oh, Ernest Johnson. His name was Ernest... Craycart. Craycart. Yeah. Where is he? He died, too. Yeah, he's dead, too. Paul Howard, the saxophone player, is the only one living now. And he conducts the Masonic Band and the Elf Band. And the Cali player, the saxophone. And so we talked to... Don't get that recorded wrong there. Howard is nothing, no conductor, nothing. See, I get all that music you see down in my basement comes from the conductor of the Los Angeles Band, the Elf and all the other bands down there. So you think Howard isn't active in music? Howard is active. He's manager's band. He's still has the business. But F.M. Lacey is the conductor of both bands. Oh, well, I had it wrong. I know he was affiliated. He snapped on my music and I hear from Lacey each week. He's a conductor of both bands. Oh, well, I had it wrong. I know he was affiliated. He snapped on my music and I hear from Lacey each week. Lacey writes me. He's my good friend. I talked to Paul Howard.
